I fixed the bug: the `<picture>` block from the report now renders as one paragraph with the comment kept inline. It also works when the `md_in_html` extension is enabled, including inside `<div markdown="1">`.

**Cause:** in `markdown/htmlparser.py`, `handle_empty_tag` treats any comment that starts a line (up to 3 spaces of indent) as a standalone raw HTML block. It didn't check whether that line was still inside an open inline element like `<picture>`. So the comment became its own block, which closed the paragraph and started a new one after it. The same applied to other block-like empty tags such as `<!DOCTYPE>`, `<?…?>` and CDATA.

**Fix:**
- **`markdown/htmlparser.py`:** the parser now keeps a list of inline tags that have been opened but not yet closed, with where each one starts in the source. A comment that starts a line only becomes a raw block if no inline tag is still open in the current paragraph. A blank line or the start of an HTML block resets the list, so an unclosed `<span>` in an earlier paragraph doesn't affect later comments.
- **`markdown/extensions/md_in_html.py`:** this extension handles inline tags with its own code, so I made the same change there. Without it, turning on `md_in_html` brought the bug back.

Other behaviour is unchanged. For example, `text\n<!-- c -->\nmore` still puts the comment between two paragraphs, as it did before.

**Tests:** I added two tests to `tests/test_syntax/blocks/test_html_blocks.py` (the reported case, and the unclosed-tag-in-an-earlier-paragraph case) and one to `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_md_in_html.py` (comment inside a `markdown="1"` block).

Running the full suite was harder than expected, for two reasons that have nothing to do with this change:
- pytest stops during collection: `tests/test_apis.py` needs `yaml`, which isn't installed, and the project setup turns a collection warning in `test_md_in_html.py` into an error.
- The checkout isn't registered as an installed package, so short extension names like `'md_in_html'` can't be found.

So I ran the suite with unittest, mapping short extension names to `markdown.extensions.*` for that run only (no files changed). 1021 of 1022 tests pass; the only error is `test_apis`, because `yaml` is missing. `test_html_blocks.py` also passes on its own under pytest.
